WITH category_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    category,
    COUNT(*) as num_lines
  FROM budget
  GROUP BY category
),
overall_avg_lines AS (
  SELECT AVG(CAST(num_lines AS FLOAT)) as avg_lines
  FROM category_counts
),
above_avg_categories AS (
  SELECT cc.category, cc.num_lines
  FROM category_counts cc
  CROSS JOIN overall_avg_lines oal
  WHERE cc.num_lines > oal.avg_lines
),
per_line_overspends AS (
  SELECT 
    b.category,
    (b.spent - b.amount) / CAST(b.amount AS FLOAT) as relative_overspend
  FROM budget b
  WHERE b.category IN (SELECT category FROM above_avg_categories)
    AND b.amount IS NOT NULL
    AND b.amount != 0
    AND b.spent IS NOT NULL
),
category_avg_overspends AS (
  SELECT 
    category,
    AVG(relative_overspend) as avg_overspend
  FROM per_line_overspends
  GROUP BY category
)
SELECT 
  AVG(cao.avg_overspend) as avg_relative_overspend,
  AVG(CAST(aac.num_lines AS FLOAT)) as avg_num_lines,
  AVG(CAST(aac.num_lines AS FLOAT)) - (SELECT avg_lines FROM overall_avg_lines) as avg_more_lines_than_overall_avg
FROM category_avg_overspends cao
JOIN above_avg_categories aac ON cao.category = aac.category

assumptions.assumption: Budget lines with amount = 0 or NULL amount/spent are excluded from relative overspend calculation to avoid division by zero and missing values
Two-stage averaging: per-line ratios are first averaged within each category, then category averages are averaged across all above-average categories

alternatives.interpretation: One-stage overspend averaging: calculate relative overspend for each line, then average directly across all lines in above-average categories without intermediate per-category averaging
